traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md are fully implemented and verified:
- File-Level Template: ensureFileSupportsAnnotation, buildSupportsTemplateComment, and insertSupportsTemplate automatically add a file-level @supports JSDoc block when missing, using the exact placeholder format specified (docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ) plus a clear TODO line. Tests in tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts confirm the template insertion behavior and location. - Format Fixes: normalizeReqPrefixInDescription (with normalizeReqId) and handleItOrTestCall implement safe normalization of malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes: extra spaces, underscores, parentheses, and lowercase IDs are all corrected to canonical [REQ-...] format. Each case is explicitly covered by tests (spacing, underscore, lowercase, parentheses) and validated via RuleTester output. - Template Quality: The placeholder template uses generic story and requirement IDs plus an explicit TODO guidance line, matching the story’s requirements for clear placeholders indicating required developer input. - Quality Standards & Safety: Auto-fixes are restricted to comments and string literals. Shebang lines are preserved; implementation code is not touched. Fixers only run when a REQ-like ID is already present and recognizable, or when inserting a non-semantic template. When the plugin cannot be certain (e.g., no REQ prefix at all, or describe string without a recognizable story), it reports errors but provides no fixer. This satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - Integration: The rule declares meta.fixable = "code" and is written as a standard ESLint RuleModule. Tests run successfully under Jest, demonstrating the auto-fix behavior via RuleTester with eslint --fix semantics. The behavior is integrated with the existing validation logic from Story 020.0 (same rule, additional auto-fix behavior). - User Experience: Templates and normalization are deterministic, consistent, and limited to formatting concerns. The TODO text gives human-readable guidance. Tests cover both corrected and unchanged cases, confirming predictable behavior. - Error Handling: The implementation only attaches a fixer when all safety preconditions hold (auto-fix options enabled, recognizable REQ prefix, first argument is a string literal). Otherwise, it reports issues without changing code, aligning with the story’s requirement that only guaranteed-safe fixes be applied. - Documentation: user-docs/api-reference.md documents the require-test-traceability rule, explicitly referencing Story 021.0 and describing both the placeholder @supports insertion and malformed [REQ-XXX] prefix normalization, as well as the configuration options autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, and testSupportsTemplate.
Targeted and full test runs confirm that the implementation and its tests are present and passing. Therefore, the story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX is fully implemented and passes all defined criteria.
